 Louisville voters cast their ballot as early voting kicks off in Kentucky 
 Voters have until Oct. 31 to vote early without needing a reason before Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. By Rya Wooten and Ellie Compton Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 6:14 PM EDT | Updated : 16 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LOUISVILLE, Ky. (WDRB+WAVE) — Early voting in Kentucky kicked off Thursday morning, with more than 20 locations to cast a ballot in Jefferson County.
 Voters have until Oct. 31 to vote early without needing a reason before Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 The Kentucky Exposition Center is offering walk-in and drive-thru voting, which is new this year. Voters who took advantage of the drive-thru polling location said everything went smoothly Thursday, though they initially had some doubts about it.
 Kentucky Secretary of State Michael Adams was among those voting early using the walk-in option and said about a quarter of voters are taking advantage of early voting.
 The goal is to make voting more accessible. One voter said he was on his way back from a foot procedure and said the drive-thru option made it easier for him to cast his ballot.
 The option will be available from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. for three days of early voting, Oct. 29-31, and from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Election Day. Walk-in voting will also be available.
 Adams encourages voters casting straight-ticket ballots should pay attention to non-partisan races in this year’s election. Those include Louisville Metro Council, judicial and mayoral races.
 The ballot includes federal, state and local races, along with a constitutional amendment. Right now, Kentucky’s governor has the ability to grant clemency, or pardons, at any time. Amendment 1 would change the state constitution to put limits on when those pardons could happen, not allowing the governor to issue them from 60 days before an election through Inauguration Day.
 Jefferson County Clerk David Yates encourages voters to review a sample ballot before voting to know what to expect at the polls. A sample ballot can be found on the Jefferson County Clerk’s Office website. 
 The U.S. Department of Justice is calling for election monitors in Jefferson and Fayette counties on Nov. 3. Yates said Kentucky law prohibits election monitors from being inside polling places, but that he’s working with the DOJ to get more details.
 Adams said that although he doesn’t think polling locations need to be monitored because he has confidence in Kentucky conducting safe and secure elections, he has been assured that monitoring agents won’t be a distraction.
 “We’ve seen no evidence of any sort of election interference from the federal government,” he said. “I was assured months ago that ICE would not be coming and making this Minneapolis, and I see no evidence that they intend to do that whatsoever.”
 Representatives from the clerk’s office said election officials and sheriff’s deputies, when necessary, are the only people allowed to talk to voters inside a polling location.
 There are more than 20 early voting locations in Jefferson County that will be open through the weekend.
 What you need to bring to vote 
 To vote in person in Kentucky, voters must bring proof of ID issued by the state that includes the person’s name and a photograph, such as a driver’s license or student ID. 
 For more information about acceptable forms of ID, click here .
 Find your polling location 
 To access Jefferson County’s voter information website, where you can check your voter registration, election results, poll information and more, click here . To look at a sample ballot for Jefferson County’s election, click here .
 Those who live outside Jefferson County can click here to access Kentucky’s election center for polling location information and more. To find a sample ballot for your county, click here .
 Election Day for the midterm election is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. in both states.
